summary: For thirty years after 1906 the Board was mostly grading and paving this district into existence, avenue by avenue, and granting railways the spur tracks to run into its plants. It holds the city's sewage plant, its wholesale produce market and its wrecking yards, and in 2000 the Board asked the state to put a parole office somewhere else. Its Opera House has stood on Third Street since at least 1924, and the city was still protecting it in 2010. Streets were closed for the Girls' Club festival in 1973 and for the opening of the Senior Center in 1981, and in the late 1990s the Board of Supervisors came out and held its own meetings here.
